The drug is implicated in targeting ATP-sensitive potassium channels, which are subsequently targeted by 4,4'-dihydroxybenzophenone, and this compound further targets hepatocytes. Similarly, 8-azaguanine is also linked to targeting T47D cells, which are then targeted by (-)-Sophoramine, and this latter compound also targets hepatocytes. These findings collectively indicate that 8-azaguanine may exert its effects on hepatocytes via a chain of molecular interactions, starting with the ATP-sensitive potassium channel and progressing through other targets. The evidence supports a plausible pathway where 8-azaguanine could modulate cellular function in hepatocytes, potentially through ion channel regulation or other mechanisms involving the identified compounds. The integration of these targets suggests a possible role for 8-azaguanine in influencing cellular processes within hepatocytes, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the exact mechanism and therapeutic relevance.
